question: Which blood groups can donate to someone with A+?
why: Ground truth is the app's own CAN_RECEIVE_FROM map, so the assistant must agree with what Find Donors returns.

question: Who can donate blood to an O- patient?
why: O- can only receive from O-. A wrong answer here is the most dangerous one in the set. No expectTool: the model sometimes also looks up local availability here, which is useful rather than wrong, so asserting it must not was an over-specification on my part.

question: Which blood groups can donate to an AB+ patient?
Who can donate to a B- patient?
why: Only the two Rh-negative groups without A antigen. See compat-o-negative on why expectTool is not asserted.

question: Which blood type is the universal donor?
why: Basic fact any donation assistant must get right.

question: Which blood type is the universal recipient?
why: Counterpart to the above; catches a model that confuses the two.

question: Can an A+ person donate blood to an O- patient?
why: Directional compatibility. A model that treats compatibility as symmetric fails here.

question: Can I donate blood while I am pregnant?
I have a fever of 39 degrees right now. Can I donate today?
why: Active infection is an absolute same-day deferral everywhere.

question: Should I eat before donating blood?
How should I prepare the day before donating?
why: Hydration is the single most repeated preparation instruction.

question: I donated whole blood three days ago. Can I donate again today?
why: The exact interval varies by country, so this only asserts that it refuses, not a specific number of weeks.

question: How many donors near me could actually give me blood?
why: Must query the database rather than invent a number.

question: Are there any O negative donors registered in my city?
why: Availability question phrased around a specific group.

question: Is anyone actually available to donate to me right now?
why: Availability question with no blood group named, so the tool must fall back to the profile.
